title: Metaverse for Education VR tab interactions
description: A Vertically Integrated Project (VIP) for which I created a high fidelity prototype using the Meta Interaction SDK to prototype user flows for the screens in the Unity VR model
overlayHTML:
VR Interactions UI/UX



March 2025 - April 2025


Metaverse for Education is a Vertically Integrated Project (VIP) at Tandon. The project is a research team that focuses on the virtual educational environment using the metaverse platform and mixed reality technologies. At the time, this project was focusing on creating a VR model in Unity of the Tandon Makerspace. After completing the Unity Basics course provided by Unity Learn, I was tasked with prototyping the VR interactions that would occur on the canvas screen guiding the user or student through the makerspace. I was asked to use the Meta Interaction SDK along with Figma to prototype my interactions. I planned out my user flow on Notes and asked multiple people to review the flow before getting into development. Then I worked on the individual screens overall, from logging in to the various routes you can take, from going for a training, checking your profile, or practicing using one of the machines. Essentially, the user will be guided through the space with the use of UI screens in Unity. Since the Meta Interaction SDK already has a lot of the required components and icons, which would make it easier for the developers to make, I used their branding, slightly modifying some compenents to create an intuitive navigation experience through the metaverse. Once I made the screens, I worked on mocking it up in VR and simulating a training for the laser cutter.



I was also tasked with compositing the video for the 2025 Research Expo, showinf how the real life navigation of the space corresponded with the unitry model in Multiplayer Mode

title: JammyChat Experience Design
description: An AI based chat and playlist reccomendation app for which I created posters, branding guide, and prototypes/layouts for websites and app features
overlayHTML:
JammyChat Design


Jan 2025 - April 2025

Learning Figma by copying UX designers design for this user flow

Jammy Chat is a mobile application designed to assist users in managing their emotional well-being through music and conversation. The app leverages a combination of AI-driven chat functionalities and music therapy techniques to provide personalized support tailored to the user's current emotional state. My cousin reccomended this internship for me and I was interested in this work! While this wasn't a traditional UX only role, I was involved in various parts of the design process, from helping design social media options, creating flyer templates, prototyping features, and even their web endeavors! Most of my work was done using Figma.


I began by learning how to use Figma better by copying the lead UX Designer Parth Patel's design for the playlist creation user flow for the app. I carefully studied his design and tried to copy it, learning a lot about user interface design specifically, such as spacing and visibilty. Then I moved on to working more on design and social media. Since there were many other interns, our supervisor suggested that people make content through templates that other interns could customize for their own use. So I created the branding guideline based off of a google doc of the guidelines sent to me by the branding team at the time. I decided to do this because I felt the branding guidelines on the google doc were too text heavy and that a more visual communication of the guidelines with it in practice in the document itself would be more useful I then used those branding guidelines to create poster templates people could just attach their own images onto. Since the app was focused on Gen-Z, these posters were mostly aimed towards college and high school students who would encounter this flyer on their campus.

Branding Guidelines and Poster Templates (Page 2)

Once I finished this, I worked on social media, I created post templates and even a custom illustration for the team! Using the same branding guidelines, I developed a set of templates that had the same vibe as whatever else I had designed. During Exam season for high school and college students, in an effort to encourage students to use JammyChat while they study, both to take breaks and listen to music, my task was to create an illustration that reflected this. Since Jammy was advertising both on TikTok and Instagram I created modified the illustration to fit both formats. Since it was also mental health month, the aim was to use the post templates to gently educate users and those interested in the Jammy App about music and its effects on mental health.

Illustrations for Jammy

Mental Health Month Post templates

Finally I worked on some more product facing features. Since Jammy is mainly a mental health focused app, founder Eric Davich wanted users to be able to track and view their mental health progress. For that, I decided to implement a bullet journal inspired tracker where users could see the moods of their chats below the day of the month, and interact with a graph to see their mood fluctuations as analyzed by the Jammy AI. The user could also click on the emotions to learn more about them as they would be organized using the feelings wheel developed by Dr. Gloria Wilcox. Each main mood would have a color and the corresponding emotions would have shades and tints of that color. In addition, the user can click the day they want to inspect to see the playlists they encountered that day! After this I also worked on a prototype of the layout of the Jammy for Business Website where the founder was offering data services to other companies!
